outline.chapter_title: Why QLoRA? The Case for Efficient Finetuning of LLMs
outline.description: Introduce the motivation, context, and high-level ideas behind QLoRA: enabling high-fidelity finetuning of very large language models on a single GPU by combining 4-bit quantization with low-rank adapters.
subtopics: The cost of standard 16-bit finetuning for large models (e.g., >780 GB for LLaMA-65B)
Inference quantization vs training-time quantization challenges
QLoRA at a glance: 4-bit base, BF16 compute, LoRA updates only
Guanaco models: performance highlights (e.g., 99.3% of ChatGPT on Vicuna)
Accessibility and democratization of LLM finetuning
Contributions overview: NF4, Double Quantization, Paged Optimizers
Key empirical claims: matching 16-bit finetuning performance

outline.description: Provide the theoretical and practical basics of quantization needed to understand QLoRA.
subtopics: Quantization and dequantization: concepts and notation
Block-wise k-bit quantization: motivation and mechanics
Outliers and why block-wise scaling helps
Quantization constants (scales) and storage overhead
Choosing ranges and zero-points
Trade-offs: precision, blocksize, memory footprint
Quantization for inference vs for training

outline.description: Explain PEFT methods with a focus on LoRA, its math, and how it reduces memory while preserving performance.
subtopics: Motivation for PEFT in LLMs
LoRA formulation: factorized adapters and scaling
Backpropagation through frozen weights to adapters
Where to place adapters: attention and MLP layers
Memory accounting: parameters vs activations vs gradients
Gradient checkpointing and its impact
Why using more adapters matters more than r in practice

outline.chapter_title: The QLoRA Method: Architecture and Training Loop
outline.description: Detail how QLoRA combines 4-bit storage, BF16 compute, and LoRA adapters into a single training pipeline.
subtopics: Separation of storage dtype (4-bit) and compute dtype (BF16)
Dequantize-on-use for forward and backward passes
Only adapter gradients computed; base weights remain frozen
Layer-wise integration: adapters across all transformer blocks
Memory profile vs 16-bit finetuning
Compatibility with popular toolchains (Transformers, bitsandbytes)
End-to-end training pipeline overview

outline.description: Present NF4, a 4-bit data type tailored for normally distributed weights, and why it outperforms FP4/Int4.

outline.description: Explain how quantizing quantization constants reduces memory overhead without sacrificing accuracy.
